answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make trust mature slowly, the way timber seasons before it bears weight. Each new identity starts on a thin trellis of permissions: small, verifiable jobs only. Limits widen only after a long streak of honest, on-time work, so calendar time and proven history, not account count, unlock full rewards. A flood of fresh identities is like shale - plentiful but brittle, splitting under sustained scrutiny - while seasoned agents keep earning.
